'''Pedro Miguel Etxenike Landiribar''', also known as '''Pedro Miguel Echenique''' (born 8 June 1950, [[Isaba]], [[Navarre]]), is a [[Basques|Basque]] theoretical [[Solid-state physics|solid-state]] physicist, Professor of [[Condensed matter physics|Condensed Matter Physics]] at the [[University of the Basque Country]] (UPV/EHU), and former minister of the [[Basque Autonomous Community]].

== Early life and education ==
Etxenike was the son of a medical doctor, Pedro Etxenike, and a teacher, Felisa Landiribar.<ref name="Jotdown2016">{{cite journal |url=https://www.jotdown.es/2016/09/pedro-echenique-cientificismo-pensar-la-ciencia-la-unica-fuente-conocimiento-verdadero-error/ |title=Pedro Echenique: "El cientificismo, el pensar que la ciencia es la única fuente de conocimiento verdadero, es un error" |author=Juan José Gómez Cadenas, Francesc Monrabal |journal=Jot Down |language=es |date=September 2016 |access-date=2019-04-18}}</ref> Growing up with one brother and one sister in a small navarrese village (with about 800 inhabitants at the time) he later attended a [[Order of Friars Minor Capuchin|Capuchin]] boarding school <ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.unavarra.es/digitalAssets/118/118912_100000001.pdf |title=Acceptance speech on the occasion of receiving the honorary degree of the Universidad Pública de Navarra |date=2008-06-13 |language=es |author=P.M. Etxenike}}</ref> He attended the [[University of Navarre]] and graduated in physics in 1972, receiving the Special Degree Prize and End-of-Studies Award.<ref name="CVcomplete"/>

In 1973, he began his studies at the [[University of Cambridge]] with a [[Fundación Juan March|March stipend]]. In 1976, he obtained his Ph.D. (with a thesis directed by [[John Pendry]])<ref>{{cite thesis |url=https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.454332 |title=Interaction of Energetic Particles with Surfaces |author=Echenique, P.M. |work=eTheses online |date=1976 |publisher=University of Cambridge |type=Ph.D |archive-date=6 August 2020 |access-date=18 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806133851/https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.454332 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and, in 1977, he received<ref>{{cite book |title=Tesis doctorales: 1976/77–1988/89. Ciencias y técnica |volume=2 |editor=Consejo de Universidades, Ministerio de Educación |date=1990 |page=205 |publisher=Ministerio de Educación |isbn=978-84-369-1825-0 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uH6m0ciI6PQC&dq=%22Aspectos+Estela+Cargadas%22&pg=PA250 |quote=the thesis is titled ''Aspectos de Estela en la Interacción de Partículas Cargadas con Medios Materiales''}}</ref> a doctorate in physics from the [[Autonomous University of Barcelona]], for which he received the Special Doctorate Prize.

== Career and research ==
After [[postdoctoral]] positions at the [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]] in [[Tennessee]] and as [[Nordic Institute for Theoretical Physics|Nordita]] Fellow of the [[Niels Bohr Institute]] in [[Copenhagen]] and with stays at [[Lund University]] he became professor of solid state physics at the [[University of Barcelona]] in 1978. In 1980, he stepped down from this position to join the [[Basque Government|government of the Basque Autonomous Region]]. In 1984, he returned to academia as a visiting lecturer at the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] in Cambridge. In 1986, he moved back to his native [[Basque Country (greater region)|Basque Country]] as professor of [[condensed matter physics]] at the [[University of the Basque Country]] (UPV/EHU) at its campus in [[San Sebastián|Donostia / San Sebastián]]. Since 1999 he is also president of the Donostia International Physics Center (DIPC).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dipc.ehu.eus/en/dipc/organizational-chart |title=Organizational chart |work=dipc.eus |access-date=2025-10-03}}</ref>

Etxenike has co-authored over 400 scientific articles.<ref name="FPA">{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.es/citations?user=HCDBpxwAAAAJ&hl=en |title=profile Pedro M. Echenique |work=Google Scholar |access-date=2019-04-17}}</ref> His research has focused on explaining the behaviour of solid bodies and their interaction with beams of charged particles. His work has opened new lines of research and has stimulated innovative theoretical and experimental lines of work in very diverse fields of condensed matter physics such as electron and tunnel microscopy, physical chemistry on the femtosecond scale, electronic surface localization, reverse photo-emission, atomic collisions, the interaction of ions with plasma particles, ion implantation and surface excitations in superfluid helium.<ref name="fpa">{{cite web|url=http://www.fpa.es/en/princess-of-asturias-awards/laureates/1998-emilio-mendez-perez-and-pedro-miguel-echenique-landiribar.html?texto=trayectoria&especifica=0 |title=Emilio Méndez Pérez and Pedro Miguel Echenique Landiríbar Prince of Asturias Award for Technical & Scientific Research 1998 |work=fpa.es |date=1998 |access-date=2019-04-17}}</ref>

Many works, starting with his PhD thesis in Cambridge study the interaction of electrons, atoms, and ions with surfaces. An important concept introduced and developed by Etxenike are ''image-potential states'' at metal surfaces <ref>{{cite journal |journal=J. Phys. C: Solid State Phys. |title=Image-potential-induced surface states |author=P.M. Echenique |volume=18 |page=L1133 |date=1985 |doi=10.1088/0022-3719/18/36/004}}</ref> in which electrons can be trapped in the potential of their own [[Method of image charges|image charge]]. Etxenike and co-workers computed and analyzed these states for many different materials and surfaces as well as their interaction with surface excitations such as [[surface plasmon]]s, [[surface plasmon polariton]]s, and [[surface phonon]]s. Etxenike is co-author of a highly cited review on the theory of surface plasmons.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Theory of surface plasmons and surface-plasmon polaritons |first1=J.M. |last1=Pitarke |first2=V.M. |last2=Silkin |first3=E.V. |last3=Chulkov |first4=P.M. |last4=Echenique |date=2006 |journal=Rep. Prog. Phys. |volume=70 |issue=1 |pages=1–87 |doi=10.1088/0034-4885/70/1/R01|arxiv=cond-mat/0611257 |bibcode=2007RPPh...70....1P |s2cid=46471088 }}</ref>

They analyzed theoretically the technique of [[Scanning tunneling microscope|scanning tunneling microscopy]] (STM) in order to interpret STM images and, in particular, relate them to the topography of the studied surfaces and to the [[spectroscopy]] of surface states ("''scanning tunneling spectroscopy''").<ref>{{cite journal |title=Theoretical aspects of scanning tunneling microscopy |first1=E. |last1=Louis |first2=F. |last2=Flores |first3=P.M. |last3=Echenique |date=1988 |journal=Phys. Scr. |volume=37 |issue=3 |pages=359–369 |doi=10.1088/0031-8949/37/3/010|bibcode=1988PhyS...37..359L }}</ref>
Etxenike has directed 27 PhD theses.<ref name="CVcomplete">{{cite web |url=https://etxenike.dipc.org/admin/documentos/archivos/cv/cvIngles.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae - Pedro Miguel Echenique Landiríbar |work=dipc.eus |date=2016 |access-date=2019-04-17 |archive-date=12 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230612111435/https://etxenike.dipc.org/admin/documentos/archivos/cv/cvIngles.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He has been very active in recent years, giving numerous lectures in different university, cultural and business forums, at which he has always defended the cultural value of scientific activity and encouraged young people to pursue science.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/advice-young-scientist |author=Elisabeth Pain |date=2015-05-12 |title=Advice to a young scientist |access-date=2019-04-17}}</ref> He co-organized outreach activities such as since 2010 the triennial festival "''Passion for Knowledge''" in San Sebastián.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://p4k.dipc.org/en/about/past-events/ |title=About Passion for Knowledge: Past events |website=p4k.org |access-date=2026-10-14}}</ref>

== Political activity ==
In 1980 he gave up his professorship in Barcelona to join the first [[Basque Government|government]] of the [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Autonomous Community]] after the [[Francoist Spain|Francoist dictatorship]]. In the government of [[Carlos Garaikoetxea]] he first served as Minister of Education and in 1983 he became minister of education and culture and spokesman for the government until the end of the legislative period in 1984. One of the milestones in this legislative period was the law on the normalisation of the use of [[Basque language|Basque]] language, for which Etxenike was the driving force and proponent. These early years of the Department of Education were also crucial in putting in place most of the foundations in the [[Basque education system|education system of the Basque Autonomous Community]], including freedom of education. The setting up of R&D centres and the internationalization of study scholarships were also promoted. {{citation needed|date=March 2024}}
 
After leaving government politics, Etxenike continues to play an important role in the science policy of the Basque Country. He was central in founding and leading a number of centers, agencies, and initiatives that are now leading research institutions in the Basque Country. He is the founder and first president of Donostia International Physics Center (DIPC), founded in 1999. He was a promoter and creator of the mixed [[Spanish National Research Council|CSIC]]-UPV/EHU centre, the [[Centre for Materials Physics]] (CFM) and was its first director (1999–2001) and is still president of the ''Materials Physics Center'' associated with CFM.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bercmpc.org/index.php/en/home/governance |title=Governance |editor=bercmpc.org |access-date=2019-04-18 |archive-date=21 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230921153724/https://bercmpc.org/index.php/en/home/governance |url-status=dead }}</ref> He played a similar role for the nanoscience research center ''CIC nanoGUNE'' (founded 2009)<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.noticiasdegipuzkoa.eus/2019/01/27/sociedad/todos-entendieron-que-no-podiamos-ahorrar-en-futuro |journal=Noticias de Gipuzkoa |title=Todos entendieron que no podíamos ahorrar en futuro |author=Mikel Mujika Iker Azurmendi |date=2019-01-27 |language=es |access-date=2019-04-18 |archive-date=27 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190127154011/https://www.noticiasdegipuzkoa.eus/2019/01/27/sociedad/todos-entendieron-que-no-podiamos-ahorrar-en-futuro}}</ref> and was until 2019 chairman of its governing board.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nanogune.eu/sites/default/files/inline-files/activity_report_19-20_en_0.pdf |title=Activity Report 2019-2020 |editor=CIC nanoGUNE |page=132 |access-date=2023-10-13}}</ref>

In 2007, he was among the founders of the Academy of Sciences, Arts and Letters of the Basque Country [[Jakiunde]] and served as its first president until 2012. He then was named honorary chairman.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.jakiunde.eus/miembros/m/?mid=38&n=Etxenike-Landiribar-Pedro-Miguel |title=Etxenike Landiribar, Pedro Miguel |publisher=Jakiunde |language=es |access-date=2018-02-15 |archive-date=18 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230618124314/https://www.jakiunde.eus/miembros/m/?mid=38&n=Etxenike-Landiribar-Pedro-Miguel |url-status=dead }}</ref>
Other positions held include membership of the governing board of the CSIC ([[Spanish National Research Council]]) (2001–2007), deputy chairperson of the board of the Franco-Spanish Euskampus Foundation,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://euskampus.eus/en/foundation/patron-en |title=Board |editor=euskampus.eus |access-date=2019-04-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190418221251/https://euskampus.eus/en/foundation/patron-en |archive-date=2019-04-18}}</ref> and vice-chairmanship of the innovation agency of the Basque government, ''Innobasque'' (2008–2012). Since 2012 he chairs the panel of judges of the Princess-of-Asturias-Prize for Scientific and Technical Research.<ref name="CVcomplete"/>
